summary: Proposes Multi-Rollout On-Policy Distillation (MOPD), a post-training method where the self-teacher is conditioned on successful and failed peer rollouts for the same prompt, giving denser token-level supervision than verifier rewards alone. Evaluated with Qwen3-4B/8B on LiveCodeBench v6, AIME/HMMT math, SciKnowEval and ToolAlpaca against base, GRPO and SDPO.

claims.claim: MOPD consistently improves over standard on-policy baselines across code, math, science QA and tool use.
claims.evidence: §5.2 and Tables 1, 4, 5; e.g. Qwen3-8B on LCBv6 reaches 61.82 mean@8 / 67.23 pass@8. No seeds or standard deviations reported for training runs.

claims.claim: Mixed success-failure peer contexts align teacher scores better with verifier rewards.
claims.evidence: §5.3 teacher-signal metrics (Spearman, Kendall, pairwise accuracy, AUC; Appendix A).

claims.claim: The '2 success + 1 failure' peer context is best.
claims.evidence: Peer-context ablation table: 2 success + 1 failure gives 61.82/67.23 on LCB, exactly the headline number, suggesting the configuration was selected on the evaluation benchmark itself (no separate validation split described).

patterns.note: Model post-training method; gains over GRPO/SDPO on verifiable tasks, small Qwen3 models only.
Relies on a verifier (tests/compiler for code) to partition rollouts into success/failure.

methodology.sample: LCBv6 131 problems; AIME2024/2025, HMMT25; SciKnowEval L3 subsets; ToolAlpaca; DeepMath 57K training examples.
methodology.baselines: Base model, GRPO, SDPO with fixed rollout budget.
methodology.variance: mean@8/pass@8 sampling metrics; no training seeds or confidence intervals.
methodology.ablations: Peer-context composition (number of successes/failures), time cost.
methodology.contamination_controls: LCBv6 chosen as problems released Feb-May 2025; otherwise none.
methodology.languages: Competitive programming code (language not emphasised), math, science, tool calls.

biases.detail: Single training run per configuration; no seeds/CIs.
Peer-context configuration appears selected on the same LCB test set used for headline results.
Contest problems and math competitions, not repository-level software engineering.

coi.affiliations: Carnegie Mellon University, Microsoft (Xiaomin Li, Haixin Wang, Gaurav Mittal, Yu Hu; Weichen Yu dual-affiliated), Purdue University. Regex vendor-hit list was empty but Microsoft affiliation is present in the author block.
coi.detail: Vendor-affiliated co-authors, but no vendor product evaluated.

verdict_reason: off-topic: model post-training/distillation method for small open models; no bearing on agent harness design, and evaluation lacks seeds with config apparently tuned on test benchmark.
applicability: Does not transfer. A Java backend team building a healthcare-education ingestion harness across ≥4 repos on mixed hosted agent hosts will not post-train Qwen3-scale models; harness, spec-driven, and cross-repo decisions are unaffected. Only tangential idea: showing an agent prior failed and successful attempts as context - but this paper tests it as a training signal, not as a prompt-time harness technique.
